question:
A convenience store plans to open several chain stores in a new residential area in the northwest suburbs of the city. To facilitate shopping, the distance from any residential area to one of the chain stores should not exceed $800 \mathrm{~m}$. Table 5-1 gives the newly built residential areas and the various areas within a radius of $800 \mathrm{~m}$ of each residential area. How many chain stores should the supermarket build in the above-mentioned areas and in which areas should they be built?
Table 5-1
\begin{tabular}{c|c}
\hline Area Code & Areas within $800 \mathrm{~m}$ radius \\
\hline A & A C E G H I \\
B & B H I \\
C & A C G H I \\
D & D J \\
E & A E G \\
F & F J K \\
G & A C E G \\
H & A B C H I \\
I & A B C H I \\
J & D F J K L \\
K & F J K L \\
L & J K L \\
\hline
\end{tabular}

    "AREAS": ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F", "G", "H", "I", "J", "K", "L"],
    "RADIUS_COVER": {
        "A": ["A", "C", "E", "G", "H", "I"],

        "I": ["A", "B", "C", "H", "I"],

        "K": ["F", "J", "K", "L"],
        "L": ["J", "K", "L"],
    },
}


def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    model.I = pyo.Set(initialize=d["AREAS"], ordered=True)
    model.J = pyo.Set(initialize=d["AREAS"], ordered=True)

    model.y = pyo.Var(model.I, within=pyo.Binary)

    def obj_rule(m):
        return sum(d["COST"] * m.y[i] for i in m.I)

    model.obj = pyo.Objective(rule=obj_rule, sense=pyo.minimize)

    def cover_rule(m, j):
        return sum(m.y[i] for i in d["RADIUS_COVER"][j]) >= 1

    model.cover = pyo.Constraint(model.J, rule=cover_rule)

    return model

#        y[i] = 1 if a chain store is built in area i, else 0.

# Objective (minimize):

#
# Constraints:
#   (1) Coverage (source: "the distance from any residential area to one of
#       the chain stores should not exceed 800 m"): for every residential
#       area j, at least one store must be built in an area that lies within
#       800 m of j.  sum_{i in cover[j]} y[i] >= 1  for all j.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

DATA = {
    # Candidate areas (rows of Table 5-1)
    "AREAS": ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F", "G", "H", "I", "J", "K", "L"],
    # Residential areas that must be covered (same set as candidate areas)
    "POINTS": ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F", "G", "H", "I", "J", "K", "L"],
    # Coverage lists from Table 5-1: for each area, the areas within 800 m
    "COVER": {
        "A": ["A", "C", "E", "G", "H", "I"],
        "B": ["B", "H", "I"],
        "C": ["A", "C", "G", "H", "I"],
        "D": ["D", "J"],
        "E": ["A", "E", "G"],
        "F": ["F", "J", "K"],
        "G": ["A", "C", "E", "G"],
        "H": ["A", "B", "C", "H", "I"],
        "I": ["A", "B", "C", "H", "I"],
        "J": ["D", "F", "J", "K", "L"],
        "K": ["F", "J", "K", "L"],

    },
    # Cost of building one store (unit cost -> minimize number of stores)
    "COST": 1,
}


def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    # Sets
    model.AREAS = pyo.Set(initialize=d["AREAS"])
    model.POINTS = pyo.Set(initialize=d["POINTS"])

    # Decision variables: build a store in area i or not
    model.y = pyo.Var(model.AREAS, within=pyo.Binary)

    # Objective: minimize total number of stores built
    def obj_rule(m):
        return sum(d["COST"] * m.y[i] for i in m.AREAS)

    model.obj = pyo.Objective(rule=obj_rule, sense=pyo.minimize)

    # Constraint (1): every residential area must be covered by at least one store
    def cover_rule(m, j):
        return sum(m.y[i] for i in m.AREAS if j in d["COVER"][i]) >= 1

    model.cover = pyo.Constraint(model.POINTS, rule=cover_rule)

    return model

    model.y = pyo.Var(model.AREAS, within=pyo.Binary)

    # z = total number of stores built (auxiliary integer)

    model.total_link = pyo.Constraint(rule=rule_total)

    # Coverage: each residential area j must be covered by at least one store
    def rule_cover(m, j):
        return sum(m.y[i] for i in m.AREAS if j in cover[i]) >= 1
    model.cover = pyo.Constraint(model.AREAS, rule=rule_cover)
